features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or degree attainment presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is stated, or the educational background is unclear.
States a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical preparation in a relevant technical field.
States a master's degree in a relevant technical field.
States a doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct design or ownership experience with agent-based systems, especially bounded autonomy and supporting control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical strength with data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has real production experience with AI systems and treats reliability, evaluation, and failure modes seriously.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as a collaborative, user-centered way to help developers and partner teams work safely with less friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with named systems, mechanisms, metrics, or outcomes.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade Go appears in the applicant's backend experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a clear, connected case for fit rather than a checklist of disconnected qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable, individual, and purposefully framed the letter feels beyond a generic template.

levels.descriptor: Highly formulaic prose with little individual voice.
Competent but generic prose with only limited individuality.
Includes a memorable framing device, belief, or personal thesis.
Sustains a distinctive, authentic voice throughout while still serving the application's purpose.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary software work, such as CTFs or similar offensive exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures the extent of public code contribution, maintenance, or responsibility for software used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and systems depth of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production track record
features.description: Captures the breadth and depth of hands-on responsibility for shipping, operating, and owning production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Professional tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade Python appears in the applicant's experience with services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Reliability and rigor mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, correctness, failure handling, operational care, and a high quality bar for long-lived systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives little signal about quality, testing, reliability, or maintainability.
The letter gestures at seriousness or standards, but without concrete habits or practices.
The letter clearly emphasizes dependable systems, testing, maintainability, guardrails, or careful design.
The letter strongly signals security-critical rigor, with explicit habits such as typed or tested tooling, auditable boundaries, reliability-first design, or builder-quality standards.

features.name: Role-specific alignment
features.description: Captures how explicitly the letter maps the applicant's background and motivation to this exact role's stated requirements and responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The fit is vague and the reader must infer most of the relevance.
Some relevant matches are stated, but the mapping to the posting is incomplete or indirect.
Clearly connects several experiences to the role's stated needs.
Makes the match easy to verify, systematically covering most of the key qualifications or responsibilities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses and validating or following through on fixes.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the team's core mission as scaling security work through automation, triage, agents, and other high-leverage systems.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the strength and relevance of formal third-party security credentials cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering mindset
features.description: Captures the maturity of the applicant's security-specific reasoning, values, and professional identity beyond generic interest in security.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the mechanical correctness and surface professionalism of the letter's spelling, grammar, and copy-editing.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to the recurring constructs above.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.
